subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood + Acme Enterprise
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@acme-enterprise.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@acme-enterprise.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood + Acme Enterprise

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our 45-minute discovery so we have a shared record and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Pain points you called out:
- Inconsistent generation latency on peak traffic (spikes causing downstream request timeouts)
- High per-token cost from current provider when traffic is bursty
- Need for stronger data controls and evidence for security/compliance (SOC 2 + data residency) for your enterprise customers

Current stack / setup you described:
- In-house model proxy layer that routes to a mix of cloud GPU endpoints and some outside vendor endpoints
- Terraform + Kubernetes for infra orchestration; SSO through Okta
- Evaluation workstreams: infra team (Tom), procurement/legal (Samantha), ML infra (two ICs)

Success criteria you’re measuring this quarter (as discussed):
- Demonstrably lower p95 token latency for inference (~target: median improvement and more consistent tail behavior)
- Predictable unit economics (monthly committed cost with clear burst/overage rules)
- Security/compliance answers + evidence (SOC 2 audit report, data access logs, KMS integration)

Initial commercial / procurement framing (so we’re aligned on what procurement will expect):
- Decision process: procurement + legal sign-off, followed by infra/security technical review; typical timeline for similar accounts we’ve seen is 4–8 weeks from formal RFx to PO if no major legal issues
- Stakeholders to engage: Samantha (Procurement/Legal), Tom (Infra/Platform), VP Eng (exec sponsor — we expect they’ll want a short product ROI slide)
- Guardrails we recommend for next steps: propose a 90-day POC on Dedicated capacity with an optional 12-month committed contract; ballpark initial TCV for sizing/procurement conversations: $150k–$300k depending on committed QPS and retention SLA

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share a short discovery recap doc (attached) and a procurement checklist for your team to review — please confirm any missing stakeholders.
2) Sam — can you confirm your formal procurement timeline and any required docs (NDA, vendor packet)?
3) Tom — can we schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive next week to map traffic patterns and target latency SLOs?

Attachments: redwood-discovery-recap-acme.pdf (summary + suggested POC config)

If you’re OK with the framing above I’ll follow up with a one-page POC proposal and a draft commercial guardrail so procurement has something to react to.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and good call. A couple internal notes on commercial framing before you send pricing:
- Let's propose a 90-day POC on Dedicated capacity with an option to convert to a 12-month committed contract. For procurement conversations, use a mid-range TCV of $200k as the starting ask; provide clear line items for committed QPS, burst rates, and logging/retention add-ons.
- Offer an introductory POC discount tier (e.g., 20% off list for the first 90 days) so procurement can justify the spend to execs.
- Make sure the proposal includes SOC 2 evidence and a data-residency statement (we can provide SOC 2 report and KMS integration doc).

Also, include a short procurement checklist (I’ve attached a template) and a link to our standard NDA so Sam can get that in place quickly.
